title: Reoadmap
text:
The items listed here are all planned features. Generally anything listed here is guaranteed to make it into a future versions. Priority is mostly based on what I feel the need to add. If you see a feature you’d like to be added sooner let me know on GitHub.

Add advanced element selector mode

Type casting for extracted data.
Add simple filters
HTML tree viewer

Improver error reporting on failed selectors.
Improve JSON display component (ResultsViewer + SavedLibrary)
Add apify actors as alternate client for ScrapeConfig.
Improved status tracking and logging.
Add settings page to extension.
Improved error recovery when network fails.
Improve selector guessing algorithm.
Add Chrome version of extension
Add online registry for ScrapeConfigs
Add tests
Add mustache based custom output formats

title: Scrape Configuration Reference

title: Scraping Fortune 500 companies executive team
text:
In this example we’ll be scraping data for Fortune 500 companies from 50Pros. More specifically we’ll be scraping the executive teams for all the companies.



50Pros Fortune 500


The first step is taking a look at the website to figure out the layout and identifying the information we want to obtain.
For this website the executive team for each company is revealed when the company row is clicked. We can do this by running the following snippet in the browser console
document.querySelectorAll('.group').forEach((el) => {el.click();})
The final config is below:
Download Config
{
  "id": "50pros.com__fortune500__ad270a6e",
  "schemaVersion": "2.0.0",
  "revision": 1,
  "url": "https://www.50pros.com/fortune500",
  "createdAt": "2026-03-21T13:19:22.112Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-03-21T13:19:22.112Z",
  "selectors": [
    {
      "id": "g_E60uqc",
1      "container": "td[colspan=\"9\"] .grid > div",
      "fields": [
        {
          "id": "f_8gaIvs",
          "name": "Role",
          "selector": ".font-bold",
          "type": "single",
          "extract": "text",
          "required": false
        },
        {
          "id": "f_5zx_hr",
          "name": "Person Name",
          "selector": " div .text-sm",
          "type": "single",
          "extract": "text",
          "required": false
        },
        {
          "id": "f_fhIqid",
          "name": "Position Name",
          "selector": " div .text-xs",
          "type": "single",
          "extract": "text",
          "required": false
        },
        {
          "id": "f_qn54EZ",
          "name": "Company Name",
2          "selector": "../../../../preceding-sibling::tr[1]/td[2]/a/text()",
          "type": "single",
          "extract": "text",
          "required": false
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "options": {
    "waitforNetworkIdle": true,
    "scrollToBottom": false,
    "runJavaScript": true,
    "pageDelayMs": 3000,
    "timeoutMs": 60000,
    "maxRetries": 2,
    "appendData": true
  },
  "pagination": {
    "mode": "none"
  },
  "output": {
    "format": "json",
    "mergeStrategy": "join",
    "flatten": true
  }
}

1

We define a container selector (line 14) in this case because the information for each executive team member is encapsulated in a recognizable DOM element. The rest of the fields are can be obtained using the interactive picker or directly inspecting the relevant parts of the page.

2

The “Company Name” (lines 32-35) field requires special attention. Since we have defined a container element, we use an XPath selector to go up in the document tree.








Note



We use a relative axis to go up in the tree before using preceding-sibling which selects siblings of the current node within the same parent. In our particular case we find the first tr element that’s before the current node after navigating up in the tree.

Member Profile Main

Since we need to extract multiple pieces of data from each page, we make use of selector groups. By default the extension starts with a single group and additional ones can be created using the No. 5 button as shown in the UI overview page.

title: Getting Started
text:
You can install PageSieve from the Mozilla Add-on Store or by downloading the latest release from GitHub.


To build the extension from source:

Clone the repository
Install dependencies: bun install
Build the project: bun run build
Load the dist/ folder as a temporary extension in your browser.

title: Getting Started
text:
You can install PageSieve from the Mozilla Add-on Store or by downloading the latest release from GitHub.


To build the extension from source:

Clone the repository
Install dependencies: bun install
Build the project: bun run build
Load the dist/ folder as a temporary extension in your browser.

title: Getting Started
text:
Basic Usage

Open the PageSieve sidebar from your browser’s extension menu.
Define Fields: Add field names for the data you want to extract.
Select Elements: Use the point-and-click selector to identify the elements on the page.
Pagination: Configure how the extension should navigate to the next page (optional).
Extract: Click the “Scrape” button to start the process.
Export: Download your results in JSON, CSV, or other supported formats.

title: Welcome to PageSieve
text:
PageSieve is a browser extension for declarative web scraping. It allows you to define field names and CSS or XPath selectors to extract structured data from any website you visit.
Get it on the Mozilla Addon Store. Star it on Github.

title: Welcome to PageSieve
text: Demo

title: Welcome to PageSieve
text:
Key Features

Point-and-click selection: Easily discover CSS selectors for any element.
Minimal Sidebar UI: No need to leave your current tab.
Local-first: All scraping is performed entirely within your browser.
Reusable Recipes: Save and share your scrape configurations as JSON files.

title: Contributing
text: Contributions are welcome! This page provides information on how to set up the development environment and contribute to PageSieve.

title: Contributing
text:
Development Setup

Clone the repository: git clone https://github.com/julius383/PageSieve.git
Install dependencies: bun install
Start the build process: bun run build:extension (for production)

title: Contributing
text:
Build Commands

bun run build:extension: Generates the production extension in the dist/ folder.
bun run lint: Runs ESLint to check for code quality issues.
bun run format: Formats the codebase using Prettier.

title: Contributing
text:
Just Tasks
If you have just installed, you can use the following commands:

just build-extension: Build the extension.
just watch: Start file watcher to trigger rebuild extension
just lint: Lint the codebase.
just format: Format the codebase.

title: Contributing
text:
Submitting Changes

Fork the repository.
Create a new branch for your changes.
Commit your changes and push them to your fork.
Submit a pull request with a clear description of your changes.

title: Architecture
text: PageSieve is designed to be local-first, ergonomic, and reusable. This page provides a high-level overview of the project’s architecture and its core components.

title: Architecture
text:
Tech Stack
The extension is built using:

TypeScript: Ensuring type safety across the codebase.
Svelte: Used for the sidebar and full-page dashboards.
Vite: The build tool and development server.
Shadcn UI: For building consistent and accessible UI components.
XState: For implementing main loop of extension.
Zod: Defining and validating scrape configurations and other schemas.

title: Architecture
text:
Core Components

Sidebar UI (packages/extension/ui/sidebar): The main interface for defining scrape configurations.
Content Script (packages/extension/src/content.ts): Injected into the webpage to interact with the DOM.
Background Script (packages/extension/src/background.ts): Manages messaging between different parts of the extension.
Scraping State Machine (packages/core/src/scrapeMachine.ts): state machine controlling main loop of the extension
DOM Inspector (packages/extension/src/dominspector.mts): Handles the click-based selection of elements.
Selector Engine (packages/extension/src/selectorgadget.ts): Implements the CSS selector guessing algorithm. Vendored version of cantino/selectorgadget: Go go CSS / DOM inspection.
Data Types (packages/core/src/schema.ts): Central location for Zod schema defining the scrape configuration.
Logging System (packages/core/src/logger.ts) and (packages/extension/src/logger.ts): Structured logging using LogTape, supporting relay to local environments.

The final config is below:

{

  "schemaVersion": "2.0.0",
  "revision": 1,
  "createdAt": "2026-07-27T09:59:06.874Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-07-27T09:59:06.874Z",
  "selectors": [
    {
      "id": "g_Mg-F4G",
      "name": "Group 1",
      "container": ".leadership-grid~ .members-list .members-list--item",
      "fields": [
        {
          "id": "f_i2PBWd",
          "name": "Name",
          "selector": ".members-list--name",
          "type": "single",
          "extract": "text",
          "required": false
        },
        {
          "id": "f_iuhh5W",
          "name": "Role",
          "selector": ".members-list--representation",
          "type": "single",
          "extract": "text",
          "required": false
        },
        {
          "id": "f_DtpueE",
          "name": "Constituency",
          "selector": "strong",
          "type": "single",
          "extract": "text",
          "required": false
        },
        {
          "id": "f_Z9Wpuf",
          "name": "URL",
1          "selector": ".",
          "type": "single",
          "extract": "attribute",
          "attribute": "href",
          "required": false
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "options": {
    "waitforNetworkIdle": true,
    "scrollToBottom": false,
    "runJavaScript": true,
    "pageDelayMs": 3000,
    "timeoutMs": 60000,
    "maxRetries": 2,
    "appendData": true
  },
  "pagination": {
2    "mode": "template",
    "urlTemplate": "https://mzalendo.com/mps-performance/national-assembly/13th-parliament/?page={{page}}",
    "startPage": 1,
    "increment": 1,
    "maxPages": 8
  },
  "output": {
    "format": "json",
    "mergeStrategy": "join",
    "flatten": true
  }
}

Using . (dot/period) in a selector is used to indicate that the selector is the field references the container. So the href extracted is from the base container (.leadership-grid .members-list--item).

2
